[{"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "What is RoPON?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "3bed9eaf-1e2d-46db-88a3-2fdd0574a9e1"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

The Registry of Polar Observing Networks (RoPON) is a catalog of systems or organizations that coordinate or conduct observation and monitoring of climate or environmental phenomena, typically with data management and infrastructure such as research stations, platforms, or instrumentation (e.g., SIOS, GTN-P, and NASA ABoVE). RoPON also displays discovery portals that are not observing networks per se, but which compile and share information about observing activities and infrastructure (e.g., ARMAP, ISAAFFIK, and Polardex). RoPON encompasses the polar and subpolar regions, including regional or global networks that extend into the high latitudes.

", "id": "fa6746e0-6db4-4332-9669-4c9ac9dc5fc1"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "What are \u201cobserving assets\u201d?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "7abb2f00-10ac-45d7-90fd-7bd791f2d30d"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

RoPON presents details about \u201cobserving assets\u201d: Components of in situ observing infrastructure and activities, categorized into various \u201casset types\u201d:

sites:

fixed stations, facilities, plots, moorings, observatories, stationary platforms, supersites, community-based observations, or locations wherever repeat measurements have been made.

mobile platforms:

buoys, vessels, aircraft, floats, gliders, UAVs, AUVs, animal-borne sensors, and other mobile platforms.

projects:

Research projects, studies, and other activities typically funded or coordinated by an agency or program within a defined timeframe.

campaigns:

Scientific cruises, aircraft operations, fieldwork, and other planned routes or completed activities.

initiatives:

Coordinated ongoing efforts including organizations, networks, observing systems, and programs.

These definitions are based on a cluster analysis of terms used by networks to describe what they track, as part of the activities of POAwg to promote the interoperability of observing-related metadata for polar observing.

", "id": "0f0b387c-4590-4d27-8fe9-8455baf5a2f3"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "What is an asset-level metadata catalog?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "f2420ac2-4486-413e-8a4c-ef7720e25939"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

Many observing networks create inventories of their own research stations, monitoring sites, drifting buoys, funded projects, scientific cruises, and other types of observing assets. In other words, they compile important details \u2013 e.g. site name, project title, latitude & longitude, contact name, operating status, dates, etc. \u2013 as fields in a database, elements in metadata records, columns in a spreadsheet, or simply as a table on a webpage or PDF. Collectively these are broadly defined as \u201casset-level metadata catalogs\u201d. To facilitate information sharing, RoPON attempts to convey whether a network has one or more, whether they are enabled for viewing, if there is machine-readable access, and if so, how.

", "id": "96bef18e-97c1-4371-a7f3-3739a9a22c02"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "Why was RoPON created?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "52dbed17-3b74-44fe-8c29-51253efa8378"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

This registry was built as a step toward making observing-related information more Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (the FAIR Principles). RoPON will help to: Co-locate and optimize limited resources; better inform local communities of activities nearby; guide network assessment & planning; clarify best practices for asset-level metadata sharing; and establish a basis for harvesting, aggregation, & federated search (for a more comprehensive perspective across networks).

", "id": "74a5b0cf-a6b3-4d7d-9a26-e8fac48d8a34"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "Who created RoPON?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "c66a3375-a3a5-4325-aa97-58f2bba332c2"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

RoPON was created as a collaborative effort by the Sustaining Arctic Observing Networks initiative (SAON), the Arctic Portal, and the SAON Polar Observing Assets Working Group (POAwg). For more information, see the About page.

", "id": "cf46b28a-1f78-41e4-a75b-d3b594dddcf6"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "What are future plans for RoPON?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "607639dc-c314-47a9-9cb0-61c4df9bf8b5"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

RoPON has been released as a phase 1 version for demonstration purposes. Contingent on additional funding, this registry will be improved with: More networks; enhancements to the UI/UX; an upgraded backend for more functionality; network-level user access to populate or update records; public, machine-readable access to the RoPON database via an API; ability to harvest network information interoperably; and otherwise to make RoPON more comprehensive and responsive to meet the needs of the polar observing and data communities.

", "id": "13bb4826-15e1-4ab9-898b-46b9e987f7a1"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "How do I add my network? How do I change what is shown for my network? How do I provide feedback?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "ea2def56-337c-4213-ae30-ae96eda3d1aa"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

Please reach out via the Contact page. Additions, edits, and suggestions are greatly appreciated! (Because RoPON is currently in phase 1, please also be patient as it may take time for changes to be enacted).

", "id": "2580a80a-0658-4467-9bb1-bc5baeff2436"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "Why aren\u2019t there more networks in RoPON?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "4431e81e-4da9-4d12-8757-a52f6f94b8fd"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

In this phase 1 version, the information for each network is manually curated by \u201cscreenscraping\u201d and data wrangling from network websites. More networks will be added as feasible while we seek additional funding. The end goal is to have a sustainable resource that is distributed and interoperable.

", "id": "e7c1c38f-b2f4-43a0-a447-41f4c0f85d95"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "What do all of the various details mean (domains, disciplines, asset types, metadata standards, etc.)? Ie., are there definitions for the terms shown on RoPON?", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "c8a44102-7af1-48bc-a201-2511e7afa473"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

Yes! RoPON and its underlying database are structured with a network-level metadata model released by the SAON Polar Observing Assets Working Group (POAwg). Feel free to download and view it to see field definitions, controlled vocabularies for various elements, and more.

", "id": "21d8db53-93d1-47d8-82c8-6c8f3efc1643"}]

[{"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "Purpose of the Registry of Polar Observing Networks \u2013 RoPON", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "cbc0c297-2c06-4bb8-b2ec-139c6a636951"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

The polar research community maintains numerous observing systems that collect observations of essential polar variables. The Polar Observing Asset working group (POAwg) provides technical guidance for sharing information about observing activities. The POAwg promotes interoperability toward a comprehensive perspective of observing activities and clarifies solutions for the deployment of interoperable, observing-related metadata catalogs. This information can then help strengthen observing systems, create knowledge maps that link observations to societal needs, and measure capacity for assessing environmental conditions.

The Polar Observing Assets working group (POAwg) facilitates the discovery and interoperability of information about research & monitoring assets in polar regions: sites, transects, observatories, projects, and networks or systems.

The POAwg was established in 2020 under the SAON Committee on Observations and Networks (CON) to reduce effort while showcasing and integrating the efforts of multiple systems.

", "id": "eba8eb7a-0f60-4625-a58a-99482c50c837"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "Goals of the POAwg:", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "8122a90d-ac98-4f8e-807b-c48f4702fc58"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

  • Make asset information more Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable
  • Promote best practices for interoperability \u201cbeyond the dataset level\u201d
  • Help span a spectrum across science planning, data management & disciplinary or interdisciplinary science
  • Create a registry of Polar observing networks, documenting asset-related metadata standards, semantic technologies, and transfer protocols in use
  • Build crosswalks and facilitate existing tools for translation across standards
  • Create recommendations for adoption and implementation of established standards and solutions

More information can be found on the POAwg website

", "id": "b0b1c065-e72b-48f0-b502-93464c922480"}]

content.title: Contact RoPON

content.body:
[{"type": "paragraph", "value": "

This web portal is the first phase of the Registry of Polar Observing Networks web portal \u2013 RoPON.

The facility is developed in cooperation between the SAON secretariat and the Arctic Portal based on the available input and collaboration from the University of Colorado (Manley) and the Polar Observing Assets working group (POAwg). The initial funding is provided by the SAON secretariat and as in-kind funding by the Arctic Portal. Further funding is being sought!

The goal of this project is to implement a database of metadata, along with a machine interface (API) and a human interface (web frontend) for accessing these data.

The deliverables of the project includes at least the following:

  • A database implementing the document \u201cMetadata Model for the Registry of Polar Observing Systems.\u201d
  • A CRUD (Create-Read-Update-Delete) API. The API should be documented through README file and through OpenAPI Specefication.
  • A web frontend implementing the \u201cRoPON\u201d document. This user interface accesses the database through the API and should allow navigating, searching, and filtering the database content and display in human-readable form.
  • A well-documented GitHub repository containing the above.

The initiative is being implemented in phases as funding is not secured yet for the complete project. The first task towards the goals is to create a Registry of Polar Observing Networks \u2013 RoPON\u2014focusing on interoperability parameters and documenting: Asset-related metadata standards (e.g., ISO 19115/19139, WIGOS, INSPIRE EF, etc.), semantic technologies (observing-related vocabularies and ontologies), transfer protocols (e.g., OAI-PMH, CSW, WFS, or custom APIs), and machine-readable endpoints that are currently in practice. Use cases for the registry have been identified and will guide the development process moving forward.

The registry will have a frontend allowing users to browse, search, and filter for networks, with a graphical interface illustrating patterns of implementation.

", "id": "f7f648c7-f788-4d73-a88d-9e34329c4f0c"}, {"type": "image", "value": 1, "id": "8e6e0af0-c8e4-44f4-bac7-f417b1b7e744"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

For further information on the technical implementation or the development plan please contact Halld\u00f3r J\u00f3hannsson \u2014 halldor@arcticportal.org

", "id": "d1e48b5d-bbea-4557-b39e-d7ee7c5f4559"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "About the Registry of Polar Observing Networks initiative", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "8283a395-aca1-4e28-9258-767408c73112"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "The Sustaining Arctic Observing Networks (SAON)", "header_level": "h3"}, "id": "6de9e88b-e943-4b98-ac6d-f648463c9f06"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

SAON is a joint initiative of the Arctic Council and the International Arctic Science Committee that aims to strengthen multinational engagement in pan-Arctic observing. The SAON process was established in 2011 at the Seventh Ministerial Meeting of the Arctic Council (AC) via the Nuuk Declaration.

SAON's vision is a connected, collaborative, and comprehensive long-term pan-Arctic Observing System that serves societal needs.

SAON facilitates, coordinates, and advocates for coordinated international pan-Arctic observations and mobilizes the support needed to sustain them.

SAON is hosted under the AMAP secretariat of the Arctic Council \u2014 arcticobserving.org

", "id": "dda6ddee-755a-4d2c-87ee-462c2b3d4bb4"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "The Polar Observing Assets working group (POAwg)", "header_level": "h3"}, "id": "651c1581-e401-41d8-8054-b454d2959119"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

The Polar Observing Assets working group (POAwg) facilitates the discovery and interoperability of information about research & monitoring assets in polar regions: sites, transects, observatories, projects, and networks or systems. The POAwg was established in 2020 under the SAON Committee on Observations and Networks (CON) to reduce effort while showcasing and integrating the efforts of multiple systems.

POAwg is led by William Manley (INSTAAR, University of Colorado).

POAwg participants represent a variety of networks and related initiatives or organizations, including: ACPS, ACTRIS, ADAC, ADC, ADIwg, AMAP, AOV, Arctic SDI, ARMAP, BOEM, CALM, CCADI, eLTER RI, EPB, ESIP, EuroARGO, GC-NET, GCW, GEO, GOOS, GTN-P, IASC/SAON ADC, ICOS, INTAROS, INTERACT, IODE, ITO, MODAAT, Nordicana D SILA, NPRB, NSIDC, OBO, PROMICE, RDA, SAON, SCADM, SIOS, SOOS, TCCON, U.S. TPC, UN Decade, US AON, and WMO.

More on the POAwg \u2014 polarobservingassets.org

", "id": "787801af-e23b-4a49-bcde-be773bb77df6"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "Arctic Portal", "header_level": "h3"}, "id": "a0c8df48-0949-4f98-81c5-95ee8bc259ce"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

ArcData\u2014Arctic Portal.org is a provider of expert web development, data and consulting services focusing on the collection, processing, evaluation, interpretation and presentation of information and data, including educational and science communication products and tools with related consulting and outreach services for business, policy makers, educators and alike.

ArcData operates the Arctic Portal.org and its IT development, outreach and data services, a comprehensive gateway to Arctic information and data on the internet, increasing information sharing and co-operation among Arctic stakeholders and granting exposure to arctic related information and data. It is a network of information and data sharing and serves as a developer and host to various websites and portals in a circumpolar context, supporting co-operation and outreach and data sharing in science, education, and policy making.

More on the Arctic Portal \u2013 arcticportal.org

", "id": "d0760366-3183-44f1-8cba-9a1f4f5d82e9"}, {"type": "heading", "value": {"heading_text": "See also", "header_level": "h2"}, "id": "c660b391-33e3-494a-8e4d-91a6a8789466"}, {"type": "paragraph", "value": "

  • A \u201cShort Statement\u201d from the Arctic Observing Summit 2022
  • A short presentation for the Polar Data Forum IV
", "id": "0ab919b5-2680-40e6-8b29-428966c4b170"}]

"}, {"id": "a0c8df48-0949-4f98-81c5-95ee8bc259ce", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h3", "heading_text": "Arctic Portal"}}, {"id": "d0760366-3183-44f1-8cba-9a1f4f5d82e9", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

ArcData\u2014Arctic Portal.org is a provider of expert web development, data and consulting services focusing on the collection, processing, evaluation, interpretation and presentation of information and data, including educational and science communication products and tools with related consulting and outreach services for business, policy makers, educators and alike.

ArcData operates the Arctic Portal.org and its IT development, outreach and data services, a comprehensive gateway to Arctic information and data on the internet, increasing information sharing and co-operation among Arctic stakeholders and granting exposure to arctic related information and data. It is a network of information and data sharing and serves as a developer and host to various websites and portals in a circumpolar context, supporting co-operation and outreach and data sharing in science, education, and policy making.

More on the Arctic Portal \u2013 arcticportal.org

[{"id": "cbc0c297-2c06-4bb8-b2ec-139c6a636951", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "Purpose of the Registry of Polar Observing Networks \u2013 RoPON"}}, {"id": "eba8eb7a-0f60-4625-a58a-99482c50c837", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

The polar research community maintains numerous observing systems that collect observations of essential polar variables. The Polar Observing Asset working group (POAwg) provides technical guidance for sharing information about observing activities. The POAwg promotes interoperability toward a comprehensive perspective of observing activities and clarifies solutions for the deployment of interoperable, observing-related metadata catalogs. This information can then help strengthen observing systems, create knowledge maps that link observations to societal needs, and measure capacity for assessing environmental conditions.

The Polar Observing Assets working group (POAwg) facilitates the discovery and interoperability of information about research & monitoring assets in polar regions: sites, transects, observatories, projects, and networks or systems.

The POAwg was established in 2020 under the SAON Committee on Observations and Networks (CON) to reduce effort while showcasing and integrating the efforts of multiple systems.

"}, {"id": "8122a90d-ac98-4f8e-807b-c48f4702fc58", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "Goals of the POAwg:"}}, {"id": "b0b1c065-e72b-48f0-b502-93464c922480", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

  • Make asset information more Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable
  • Promote best practices for interoperability \u201cbeyond the dataset level\u201d
  • Help span a spectrum across science planning, data management & disciplinary or interdisciplinary science
  • Create a registry of Polar observing networks, documenting asset-related metadata standards, semantic technologies, and transfer protocols in use
  • Build crosswalks and facilitate existing tools for translation across standards
  • Create recommendations for adoption and implementation of established standards and solutions

More information can be found on the POAwg website

"}]

[{"id": "3bed9eaf-1e2d-46db-88a3-2fdd0574a9e1", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "What is RoPON?"}}, {"id": "fa6746e0-6db4-4332-9669-4c9ac9dc5fc1", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

The Registry of Polar Observing Networks (RoPON) is a catalog of systems or organizations that coordinate or conduct observation and monitoring of climate or environmental phenomena, typically with data management and infrastructure such as research stations, platforms, or instrumentation (e.g., SIOS, GTN-P, and NASA ABoVE). RoPON also displays discovery portals that are not observing networks per se, but which compile and share information about observing activities and infrastructure (e.g., ARMAP, ISAAFFIK, and Polardex). RoPON encompasses the polar and subpolar regions, including regional or global networks that extend into the high latitudes.

"}, {"id": "7abb2f00-10ac-45d7-90fd-7bd791f2d30d", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "What are \u201cobserving assets\u201d?"}}, {"id": "0f0b387c-4590-4d27-8fe9-8455baf5a2f3", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

RoPON presents details about \u201cobserving assets\u201d: Components of in situ observing infrastructure and activities, categorized into various \u201casset types\u201d:

sites:

fixed stations, facilities, plots, moorings, observatories, stationary platforms, supersites, community-based observations, or locations wherever repeat measurements have been made.

mobile platforms:

buoys, vessels, aircraft, floats, gliders, UAVs, AUVs, animal-borne sensors, and other mobile platforms.

projects:

Research projects, studies, and other activities typically funded or coordinated by an agency or program within a defined timeframe.

campaigns:

Scientific cruises, aircraft operations, fieldwork, and other planned routes or completed activities.

initiatives:

Coordinated ongoing efforts including organizations, networks, observing systems, and programs.

These definitions are based on a cluster analysis of terms used by networks to describe what they track, as part of the activities of POAwg to promote the interoperability of observing-related metadata for polar observing.

"}, {"id": "f2420ac2-4486-413e-8a4c-ef7720e25939", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "What is an asset-level metadata catalog?"}}, {"id": "96bef18e-97c1-4371-a7f3-3739a9a22c02", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

Many observing networks create inventories of their own research stations, monitoring sites, drifting buoys, funded projects, scientific cruises, and other types of observing assets. In other words, they compile important details \u2013 e.g. site name, project title, latitude & longitude, contact name, operating status, dates, etc. \u2013 as fields in a database, elements in metadata records, columns in a spreadsheet, or simply as a table on a webpage or PDF. Collectively these are broadly defined as \u201casset-level metadata catalogs\u201d. To facilitate information sharing, RoPON attempts to convey whether a network has one or more, whether they are enabled for viewing, if there is machine-readable access, and if so, how.

"}, {"id": "52dbed17-3b74-44fe-8c29-51253efa8378", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "Why was RoPON created?"}}, {"id": "74a5b0cf-a6b3-4d7d-9a26-e8fac48d8a34", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

This registry was built as a step toward making observing-related information more Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (the FAIR Principles). RoPON will help to: Co-locate and optimize limited resources; better inform local communities of activities nearby; guide network assessment & planning; clarify best practices for asset-level metadata sharing; and establish a basis for harvesting, aggregation, & federated search (for a more comprehensive perspective across networks).

"}, {"id": "c66a3375-a3a5-4325-aa97-58f2bba332c2", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "Who created RoPON?"}}, {"id": "cf46b28a-1f78-41e4-a75b-d3b594dddcf6", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

RoPON was created as a collaborative effort by the Sustaining Arctic Observing Networks initiative (SAON), the Arctic Portal, and the SAON Polar Observing Assets Working Group (POAwg). For more information, see the About page.

"}, {"id": "607639dc-c314-47a9-9cb0-61c4df9bf8b5", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "What are future plans for RoPON?"}}, {"id": "13bb4826-15e1-4ab9-898b-46b9e987f7a1", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

RoPON has been released as a phase 1 version for demonstration purposes. Contingent on additional funding, this registry will be improved with: More networks; enhancements to the UI/UX; an upgraded backend for more functionality; network-level user access to populate or update records; public, machine-readable access to the RoPON database via an API; ability to harvest network information interoperably; and otherwise to make RoPON more comprehensive and responsive to meet the needs of the polar observing and data communities.

"}, {"id": "ea2def56-337c-4213-ae30-ae96eda3d1aa", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "How do I add my network? How do I change what is shown for my network? How do I provide feedback?"}}, {"id": "2580a80a-0658-4467-9bb1-bc5baeff2436", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

Please reach out via the Contact page. Additions, edits, and suggestions are greatly appreciated! (Because RoPON is currently in phase 1, please also be patient as it may take time for changes to be enacted).

"}, {"id": "4431e81e-4da9-4d12-8757-a52f6f94b8fd", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "Why aren\u2019t there more networks in RoPON?"}}, {"id": "e7c1c38f-b2f4-43a0-a447-41f4c0f85d95", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

In this phase 1 version, the information for each network is manually curated by \u201cscreenscraping\u201d and data wrangling from network websites. More networks will be added as feasible while we seek additional funding. The end goal is to have a sustainable resource that is distributed and interoperable.

"}, {"id": "c8a44102-7af1-48bc-a201-2511e7afa473", "type": "heading", "value": {"header_level": "h2", "heading_text": "What do all of the various details mean (domains, disciplines, asset types, metadata standards, etc.)? Ie., are there definitions for the terms shown on RoPON?"}}, {"id": "21d8db53-93d1-47d8-82c8-6c8f3efc1643", "type": "paragraph", "value": "

Yes! RoPON and its underlying database are structured with a network-level metadata model released by the SAON Polar Observing Assets Working Group (POAwg). Feel free to download and view it to see field definitions, controlled vocabularies for various elements, and more.

"}]
